reports.title: CrowdStrike Reports Third Quarter Fiscal Year 2027 Financial Results

guidance.heading: Financial Outlook
section: CrowdStrike is providing the following guidance for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027 (ending January 31, 2027) and increasing its guidance for fiscal year 2027 (ending January 31, 2027).

Q4 FY27Guidance | Full Year FY27Guidance
Annual recurring revenue | $6,712.2 - $6,716.2 million | $6,712.2 - $6,716.2 million
Total revenue | $1,638.1 - $1,644.1 million | $6,078.1 - $6,084.1 million
Non-GAAP income from operations | $438.1 - $441.5 million | $1,540.9 - $1,544.3 million
Non-GAAP net income attributable to CrowdStrike | $380.3 - $383.0 million | $1,341.6 - $1,344.3 million
Non-GAAP net income per share attributable to CrowdStrike common stockholders, diluted | $0.36 | $1.28
Weighted average shares used in computing non-GAAP net income per share attributable to common stockholders, diluted | 1,056 million | 1,046 million
Non-GAAP tax rate | 21.0% | 21.0%

desk.headline: Revenue up 28% to $1.58bn and adjusted EPS of $0.34, above estimates; full-year outlook raised as it agrees to buy Zscaler
results: Revenue rose 28% to $1.58bn, ahead of the $1.53bn analysts expected; adjusted EPS of $0.34 beat the $0.31 estimate.
Net new ARR was a record $419m, up 58%, taking total ARR to $6.26bn (+27%), the fifth straight quarter of faster growth.
Profitability improved: non-GAAP operating margin rose to 26% from 21%, and the company made a small GAAP profit of $24.9m.
Cash generation was a record: operating cash flow of $665m and free cash flow of $474m (30% of revenue); cash stood at $5.37bn.
CrowdStrike agreed to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal valuing it at about $43.9bn (1.135 CrowdStrike shares per Zscaler share).

guidance.summary: CrowdStrike raised its full-year FY27 outlook to revenue of $6.08bn and adjusted EPS of $1.28, and gave Q4 guidance of $1.64bn revenue and $0.36 EPS. The outlook excludes Zscaler.

points: Management said spending on securing new technology is lifting budgets, widening platform use and speeding up deals.
Falcon Flex, its pay-as-you-go plan, roughly doubled to over $2.79bn of ARR across more than 4,000 accounts.
The Zscaler deal is pitched as adding network security; targets are about $1bn of yearly revenue synergies within 30 months and $500m of cost savings in 18–24 months.
The deal is expected to close in the second half of fiscal 2028, subject to approvals; management admitted integration will be hard.
Excluding Zscaler, management expects net new ARR to grow at least 20% in fiscal 2028.
call.source: Call coverage: TipRanks, 25 Nov 2026; Benzinga via TradingView, 23 Nov 2026

watch: Regulatory and shareholder approval of the Zscaler deal, and the share dilution it brings.
Whether net new ARR keeps growing quickly in Q4 against the raised targets.
Subscription gross margin, which management warned may move around from quarter to quarter.
